checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-016: Does parse_deposit_requests use exact equality (==) to compare log.address against DEPOSIT_CONTRACT_ADDRESS?

audit_items.reasoning: ProcessLog (beacon-chain/execution/log_processing.go:93-108) performs only a topic-signature check (depositLog.Topics[0] == depositEventSignature) and NEVER verifies that depositLog.Address equals s.cfg.depositContractAddr. The sole address filtering is the ethereum.FilterQuery Addresses field submitted to the external EL client (httpLogger.FilterLogs), which is an untrusted party. Any compromised or malicious execution client can return FilterLogs responses containing logs from attacker-controlled contracts with the correct event topic, bypassing the address filter entirely. ProcessDepositLog then processes these fake logs — inserting the attacker's data into the deposit trie and deposit cache. This missing application-layer address check is a confirmed defense-in-depth gap in a security-critical path. Test evidence from service_test.go confirms logs with Address=common.Address{} (zero, not deposit contract) are expected to pass through ProcessLog successfully.

phase1.summary: The deposit log processing pipeline has two distinct layers: (1) ProcessETH1Block/processBlockInBatch submit FilterQuery with Addresses=[depositContractAddr] to the EL client, relying on the EL to pre-filter; (2) ProcessLog only checks the event topic (depositEventSignature), never the source address. The abstract domain for depositLog.Address entering ProcessLog is the full common.Address space — no restriction is applied at the application layer. s.cfg.depositContractAddr is immutable after initialization (set from config, stored in DB). The mutable state targets (depositTrie, depositCache, lastReceivedMerkleIndex, ChainstartDeposits) are all reachable through a spoofed log.
state_anomalies_found: ProcessLog contains no check of depositLog.Address — only depositLog.Topics[0] is validated.
ProcessDepositLog performs no address re-verification — it calls UnpackDepositLogData(depositLog.Data) directly.
The sole address filter (FilterQuery.Addresses) is enforced by the external EL client (httpLogger), not by the beacon application.
ProcessLog is an exported method on *Service — callable by any code holding a Service reference without any address pre-filtering.
processingLock.RLock is acquired in ProcessLog but mutations in ProcessDepositLog (lastReceivedMerkleIndex, depositTrie, depositCache) happen under this read lock, not a write lock.
phase1.cache_analysis: The deposit trie (s.depositTrie) and deposit cache (s.cfg.depositCache) are the primary mutable state targets. ProcessDepositLog inserts into the trie at position 'index', calls depositCache.InsertDeposit always, and InsertPendingDeposit post-genesis. Pre-genesis, deposits are also added to ChainstartDeposits and processDeposit is called, directly affecting the genesis validator set.

phase2.summary: Exploit requires supplying to ProcessLog a *gethtypes.Log with Topics[0]==depositEventSignature, correct sequential merkleTreeIndex, ABI-encoded valid deposit data, and Address set to any non-deposit-contract address. Two primary vectors: (1) compromised/malicious EL client returning crafted FilterLogs response; (2) direct Go call to s.ProcessLog() from within the beacon process.
phase2.counterexample: Attacker operates a malicious execution client at the beacon node's --execution-endpoint. When the beacon calls FilterLogs with Addresses=[depositContractAddr], the malicious EL returns logs from attacker-controlled contract at 0xDEAD... with Topics[0]=keccak256('DepositEvent(bytes,bytes,bytes,bytes,bytes)') and Data=ABI-encoded(pubkey=<attacker_key>, withdrawalCredentials=<attacker_controlled>, amount=32ETH, signature=<valid_BLS>, merkleTreeIndex=<expected_next_index>). ProcessLog passes the topic check; ProcessDepositLog decodes the data and inserts the fake deposit into the trie and cache. Pre-genesis: attacker's validator key enters genesis state. Post-genesis: fake pending deposit is queued for inclusion.
attack_scenarios: Compromised EL client injects fake genesis validator deposits by returning spoofed FilterLogs responses with attacker pubkeys.
Post-genesis: inject fake pending deposits into depositCache.InsertPendingDeposit for validators who never deposited real ETH.
Denial of service: supply a fake log with out-of-sequence merkleTreeIndex causing ProcessDepositLog to error and halt the entire deposit processing pipeline.
Deposit trie corruption: inject fake deposits to corrupt trie root, causing state root mismatches between beacon state deposit root and on-chain deposit root.
phase2.timing_dependencies: No race conditions required for the primary attack. The attacker needs to control EL client responses at any point during log processing. The sequential merkle index check (index != lastReceivedMerkleIndex+1) limits injection to one fake deposit per expected deposit slot when only partially controlling the EL; full EL control allows complete deposit sequence replacement.

phase2_5.summary: Attack is externally reachable via the EL client connection. The beacon node trusts its connected EL as a data source for log filtering. The httpLogger (bind.ContractFilterer interface) is set from the live EL connection. An attacker controlling the EL endpoint can supply spoofed log data. No gRPC, REST, or P2P endpoint directly exposes ProcessLog to external callers — network exposure is via the EL trust boundary, not direct RPC.
entry_points: httpLogger.FilterLogs response (main attack vector — requires EL client compromise or MitM)
Direct Go call to exported s.ProcessLog() from within the beacon process (internal, requires code execution)
phase2_5.attack_surface: The beacon node's trust relationship with its connected execution client. The EL client is expected to enforce the FilterQuery address filter, but this is not cryptographically guaranteed. A compromised or malicious EL at the configured --execution-endpoint can supply crafted logs bypassing this filter.

phase3.summary: The property 'deposit events are only processed from the canonical deposit contract address' (equivalently: depositLog.Address == s.cfg.depositContractAddr at the point of processing) is definitively FALSE in the current implementation. No application-layer address assertion exists in ProcessLog or ProcessDepositLog. The invariant is delegated to the external EL client, violating the principle of enforcing security-critical invariants at the point of use.
phase3.guard_identified: ethereum.FilterQuery{Addresses: []common.Address{s.cfg.depositContractAddr}} in ProcessETH1Block (line 63-66). Topic check: depositLog.Topics[0] == depositEventSignature in ProcessLog (line 97).
phase3.guard_sufficiency: INSUFFICIENT. The FilterQuery Addresses filter is enforced by the EL client (untrusted external party). ProcessLog and ProcessDepositLog contain zero address verification. The topic check (depositEventSignature) is a necessary but not sufficient condition — any contract can emit events with the same topic. The invariant is never provably satisfied at the application layer.
edge_cases: ProcessLog is exported and callable without any address pre-filtering — the function comment says it handles 'logs from the deposit contract' but does not enforce this precondition in code.
No bounds check on depositLog.Topics length before Topics[0] access — a log with zero topics would panic (index out of range), though EL clients would not return such logs in practice.
The processingLock is RLock (shared) while ProcessDepositLog mutates s.lastReceivedMerkleIndex — inconsistent lock semantics.
Post-Pectra (EIP-6110), the depositRequestsStarted flag bypasses ETH1 log-based deposit processing entirely — the vulnerability only applies to pre-Pectra deposit processing and transition period.
service_test.go explicitly uses logs with Address=common.Address{} (zero address) confirming no address validation is expected or enforced by design.

phase3_5.reason: Confirmed missing application-layer address verification in ProcessLog — the critical guard 'depositLog.Address == s.cfg.depositContractAddr' is absent. The sole protection is delegated to the untrusted EL client. Impact: fake deposit injection into deposit trie and cache (possibly genesis validators), potential deposit trie corruption, and DoS via merkle index desynchronization. Attack requires EL client compromise but represents a Critical design gap in a consensus-critical security boundary explicitly identified as a threat model concern (tb-016).
phase3_5.recommendation: Add explicit address verification as the first check in ProcessLog after lock acquisition: `if depositLog.Address != s.cfg.depositContractAddr { return nil }`. This enforces the critical invariant at the application layer independent of what the EL client returns.
phase3_5.severity_estimate: High (with EL compromise prerequisite) to Critical (in Byzantine fault model where EL is untrusted). Missing application-layer invariant in a security-critical consensus function.

checklist_item.title: Verify actor-execution-client correctly filters deposit events: Are all log sources validated before deposit event processing?

audit_items.state_context: All three code paths (ProcessETH1Block -> FilterLogs -> ProcessLog, processBlockInBatch -> FilterLogs -> ProcessLog, direct ProcessLog call) reach ProcessDepositLog without any address verification at the application layer. The FilterQuery address filter is the only protection and is enforced by the EL client, not the beacon application.
audit_items.reasoning: The property 'all log sources are validated before deposit event processing' is definitively NOT met. No address validation exists in ProcessLog (lines 91-108), ProcessDepositLog (lines 110-200+), or UnpackDepositLogData (contracts/deposit/logs.go:10-24). The full processing chain after FilterLogs returns contains zero application-layer address verification. All three call paths to ProcessDepositLog are reached without source address validation. This is a complete absence of the guard, not a weak implementation. The only partial mitigation is the sequential merkle index check in ProcessDepositLog, which limits damage when the attacker only partially controls EL responses but provides no protection when the EL client is fully compromised. The vulnerability is confirmed and matches the same root cause as CHK-W5B6-51-001.

phase1.summary: All processing paths (ProcessETH1Block, processBlockInBatch, direct ProcessLog call) reach ProcessDepositLog without address verification. The abstract state of 'which address emitted this log' is never consulted after FilterQuery is submitted. The EL client (httpLogger, bind.ContractFilterer interface) is set at runtime from the EL connection — in tests, goodLogger mock with nil backend returns logs with Address=common.Address{} (zero address) without any failure. ProcessDepositLog is the state mutation point: it modifies lastReceivedMerkleIndex, depositTrie, depositCache, and pre-genesis also ChainstartDeposits and preGenesisState.
state_anomalies_found: ProcessDepositLog: no address check — processes log.Data directly via UnpackDepositLogData.
UnpackDepositLogData: purely ABI-decodes the data field; no address validation.
No debug endpoint or gRPC handler exposes ProcessLog directly to the network — it is an internal Go exported method.
processingLock.RLock in ProcessLog allows concurrent reads while ProcessDepositLog mutates shared state (lastReceivedMerkleIndex, depositTrie, depositCache) — inconsistent lock semantics.
The depositRequestsStarted flag (EIP-6110) bypasses ETH1 log processing post-Pectra, limiting the vulnerability window to pre-Pectra deposit processing.

phase2.summary: Three distinct call paths all reach ProcessDepositLog without address verification: (a) ProcessETH1Block -> FilterLogs[addr-filter] -> ProcessLog; (b) processBlockInBatch -> FilterLogs[addr-filter] -> ProcessLog; (c) direct s.ProcessLog() call. In paths (a) and (b), the addr-filter is enforced by the EL client. In path (c), there is no pre-filtering at all. ProcessDepositLog is reached with any log whose Topics[0]==depositEventSignature and sequential merkleTreeIndex.
phase2.counterexample: Via path (a): Attacker operates malicious EL at beacon's --execution-endpoint. When beacon calls FilterLogs with Addresses=[depositContractAddr], the malicious EL returns logs from attacker contract 0xBAD... with Topics[0]=keccak256('DepositEvent(bytes,bytes,bytes,bytes,bytes)'), Data=ABI-encoded(attacker_pubkey, attacker_withdrawal_credentials, 32ETH, signature, expectedNextIndex). ProcessLog passes topic check; ProcessDepositLog inserts fake deposit into trie and cache. Pre-genesis: adds attacker validator to genesis set. This is a complete bypass of the 'deposit contract address = tb-016' trust boundary.
attack_scenarios: Pre-genesis: inject attacker validator pubkeys as genesis validators by supplying fake deposit logs with correct sequential indices before chainstart — long-range attack enablement.
Post-genesis: poison pending deposit queue with fake validators who have no real ETH on-chain — fraudulent validator activation.
DoS: supply fake log with wrong sequential merkle index causing 'received incorrect merkle index' error, halting deposit pipeline.
Trie corruption: inject fake deposits causing beacon state deposit_root to diverge from on-chain deposit root, triggering attestation failures or sync issues.
phase2.timing_dependencies: No timing or race condition required for primary attack. Sequential merkle index check limits injection rate when EL is only partially controlled; full EL control removes all rate limits.

phase2_5.summary: All three code paths confirmed to reach ProcessDepositLog without address verification. No gRPC/REST/P2P endpoint directly exposes ProcessLog as a network API — external reachability is solely via the EL trust boundary. Attack requires control of the EL endpoint configured in the beacon node.
entry_points: httpLogger.FilterLogs response (main vector — EL client compromise required)
Direct Go call to exported s.ProcessLog() (requires code execution in beacon process)
phase2_5.attack_surface: The beacon node's EL client connection. FilterQuery address filter is a best-effort hint to the EL, not an application-layer cryptographic constraint. The beacon must independently verify log source addresses to enforce the tb-016 trust boundary.

phase3.summary: The property 'all log sources are validated before deposit event processing' is definitively FALSE. No address validation exists anywhere in the processing chain after FilterLogs returns. The guard is a complete absence — not a weak implementation but a missing check. The proof of this property fails at the first check: there is no depositLog.Address comparison in ProcessLog or ProcessDepositLog.
phase3.guard_identified: None at the application layer. FilterQuery.Addresses filter is the sole guard and is enforced by the untrusted EL client.
phase3.guard_sufficiency: The guard is fundamentally insufficient. The FilterQuery Addresses filter is (1) enforced by the EL client, an external potentially untrusted party; (2) absent in any direct call path to ProcessLog; (3) not a cryptographic guarantee. Missing `depositLog.Address == s.cfg.depositContractAddr` check in ProcessLog means the invariant can never be provably satisfied at the application layer.
edge_cases: The processing chain (ProcessLog -> ProcessDepositLog -> UnpackDepositLogData) contains zero address checks — this is a complete absence of the invariant, confirmed by code inspection.
service_test.go uses logs with Address=common.Address{} (zero address) — test harness confirms the missing check is the intended behavior (no address check expected).

Post-Pectra (depositRequestsStarted=true): ETH1 log-based deposit processing is bypassed entirely via EIP-6110 system deposits from execution payload — this vulnerability only applies to the pre-Pectra deposit processing path and Pectra transition period.
The sequential merkleTreeIndex check provides partial rate-limiting but does not address the address validation gap.

phase3_5.reason: Confirmed: the property 'all log sources validated before deposit event processing' is not met. The processing chain ProcessLog -> ProcessDepositLog -> UnpackDepositLogData contains zero application-layer address verification. All call paths reach deposit state mutation without the required address check. Impact in adversarial EL model: fake deposit injection, genesis validator manipulation, pending deposit poisoning, and potential consensus state corruption. This is the same root cause as CHK-W5B6-51-001 — a systemic missing invariant across the entire deposit processing subsystem.
phase3_5.recommendation: Add `if depositLog.Address != s.cfg.depositContractAddr { return nil }` as the first check in ProcessLog (after lock acquisition). This single fix enforces the invariant for all callers of ProcessLog regardless of upstream pre-filtering. Additionally, consider adding the same check at the start of ProcessDepositLog as defense-in-depth, since ProcessDepositLog is also an exported method.
phase3_5.severity_estimate: High (requires EL compromise) to Critical (in Byzantine EL model). Systemic missing invariant across all deposit processing code paths in a consensus-critical function.
